answer: AI agent economies blunt Sybil attacks with stake-weighted identity: an agent earns reputation and voting power only by bonding capital, and that weight follows the bond rather than the count of accounts. Splitting into many sybils therefore gains nothing, since every fake identity must post its own deposit. The attacker's cost grows linearly with each new identity, and detected fraud slashes the bond, so even a nebula of bots needs a ridge of real collateral beneath it; the staked asset, whether juniper credit or plain stake, cannot be conjured for free.
